PER-CALL FINDINGS (each call was read on its own for this question; quotes verified)
CALL-014 (Verity Payments): Yes — they left mainly because the product never delivered the promised business-user autonomy: operations never built the workflows, so the account became an expensive engineering tool instead. The connector gap and support inconsistency mattered, but they were presented as contributing factors or symptoms rather than the core reason.
   [02:41] Kwame Boateng: "The connector gap was real. But it wasn't why we left."
   [02:52] Kwame Boateng: "Nobody in operations ever built anything."
   [03:19] Sarah Lindqvist: "Every one."
   [03:21] Kwame Boateng: "we paid a premium for a business-user platform and used it as an engineering tool."
   [04:31] Kwame Boateng: "by January I'd already half-concluded it wasn't going to work and I didn't want to spend my team's time on it."
   [06:19] Sarah Lindqvist: "Because we were maintaining custom integrations to a platform whose main selling point was that we wouldn't have to"
   [11:23] Sarah Lindqvist: "It's not why we left. But it contributed to a general feeling that we were a small account."
   [12:49] Sarah Lindqvist: "That's when it was over, if you want the specific moment."
CALL-015 (Oakhill Property): Yes, they left mainly because OrbitFlow was overkill and too expensive for Oakhill’s actual usage. Hazel said they bought more than they needed, the product worked fine, but the value didn’t justify the price once the original future roadmap never happened and the benefits became easy to overlook.
   [00:43] Hazel Wren: "We bought something we didn't need. That's the whole answer."
   [01:42] Hazel Wren: "They worked perfectly. That's the frustrating part. I've got no complaint about the product at all."
   [02:02] Hazel Wren: "About two thousand a year. Maybe two and a half with the tier we need."
   [03:12] Hazel Wren: "They're the three things that matter and they're worth something. They're not worth nineteen thousand pounds a year to a company our size."
   [05:27] Hazel Wren: "Yes. That's a good way of putting it. We paid for eleven workflows' worth of value and a plan for forty."
   [06:19] Hazel Wren: "There should be a smaller plan. Something for a company that needs five workflows and three users"
   [07:10] Hazel Wren: "Nothing changed. That's the thing. It kept working. But the pain it solved stopped being fresh, and the invoice kept arriving"

=== CALL-014 (call kind: churn)
CALL ID: CALL-014
DATE: 2026-09-18
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
CUSTOMER: Verity Payments
INDUSTRY: Payments
COMPANY SIZE: 800 employees
STAGE: Churn post-mortem
DURATION: 21 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Ruth Adeyemi, Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow
- Kwame Boateng, Head of Operations, Verity Payments
- Sarah Lindqvist, Engineering Manager, Verity Payments
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Kwame, Sarah — thank you for doing this. You didn't have to.
[00:05] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We nearly didn't, if I'm honest.
[00:08] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. And I want to set expectations: this isn't a save attempt. You've signed with Workato, the decision's made, and I'm not going to spend twenty minutes trying to reopen it.
[00:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Good. That was my concern.
[00:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What I want is to understand what went wrong properly, because two years is a long time to get something wrong and I'd like to not do it again.
[00:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We'll be honest then.
[00:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please be.
[00:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd add — I took over this account in January, so about eight months ago. Some of what went wrong predates me and some of it doesn't, and I'd rather you told me which is which.
[00:55] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Alright. Where do you want to start?
[00:59] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): With the decision. When did you actually decide?
[01:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Properly? June.
[01:07] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): June.
[01:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Though I'd say the decision became inevitable in about February and it took us until June to admit it.
[01:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): February.
[01:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): February.
[01:21] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a month after I took the account.
[01:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not about you. I want to be clear about that.
[01:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd still like to know what happened in February.
[01:33] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): February was when we tried to build the settlement reconciliation workflow and couldn't.
[01:40] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Couldn't, or found it hard?
[01:43] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Couldn't, in the sense that the effort exceeded the value by a factor I couldn't justify to my team.
[01:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Tell me about it specifically.
[01:54] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Our settlement provider is a mid-sized European processor. You don't have a connector for them. Nobody does, to be fair — Workato doesn't either.
[02:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So what was the difference?
[02:09] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The difference is that we ended up writing a custom integration either way, and once you've accepted you're writing custom integrations, you start asking what the platform is actually giving you.
[02:24] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And what was the answer?
[02:26] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Orchestration and run history, which are genuinely good. But not enough on their own for what we were paying.
[02:35] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): And this is where I'd push back on Sarah slightly.
[02:39] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Go on.
[02:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The connector gap was real. But it wasn't why we left. It was the thing we pointed at.
[02:49] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was the real reason?
[02:52] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nobody in operations ever built anything.
[02:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Say more.
[02:59] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The entire pitch — and this is the pitch I bought, so I'm implicating myself — was that my team would own their own workflows. That we'd stop queuing behind engineering. Two years in, every single production workflow was built by Sarah's team.
[03:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Every one.
[03:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [crosstalk] So we paid a premium for a business-user platform and used it as an engineering tool. And as an engineering tool it's fine but it's not worth the premium.
[03:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Why didn't your team build?
[03:37] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] A few reasons and none of them are flattering.
[03:42] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have unflattering.
[03:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The first workflow anyone builds is hard. Not conceptually hard — fiddly. You have to understand connections, you have to understand how data moves between steps, you have to understand what happens when something's null. My operations people are good at operations. They're not good at that, and expecting them to become good at it in their spare time was naive.
[04:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did you have enablement?
[04:13] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We had a two-day onboarding at the start. Eight people attended. Six of them never touched it again.
[04:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And after that?
[04:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nothing, until you arrived in January and offered some sessions.
[04:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Which you declined.
[04:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which I declined, because by January I'd already half-concluded it wasn't going to work and I didn't want to spend my team's time on it.
[04:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's useful and it's painful.
[04:46] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You asked.
[04:48] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I did ask. What would have changed it? If I'd arrived in month three rather than month twenty?
[04:56] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Honestly, I think if someone had sat with two of my people for a week in the first quarter and got them to ship something real, we'd still be a customer.
[05:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I agree with that.
[05:10] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Not a training course. Sitting with them. Building the actual thing they needed.
[05:17] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We do offer that.
[05:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Do you? Nobody ever offered it to me.
[05:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] It's a paid professional services engagement.
[05:28] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Ah.
[05:30] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which is possibly the problem. If the thing that makes the product succeed is a paid add-on, and the customer doesn't know they need it until it's too late —
[05:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Then you've designed a product that fails by default for people like me.
[05:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a harsher way of putting it than I would have, but I can't argue with it.
[05:53] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I add the engineering perspective? Because it's different.
[05:58] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please.
[06:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): My team quite liked it. The run history is genuinely better than what we'd have built. The exception queues are good. When something failed at three in the morning, we could see why, and that's not nothing.
[06:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So why did you support leaving?
[06:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Because we were maintaining custom integrations to a platform whose main selling point was that we wouldn't have to maintain custom integrations. And because the licence cost was being justified by a benefit — business-user autonomy — that wasn't materialising.
[06:39] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Say the other thing.
[06:41] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] And because two of my engineers wanted to build it in-house and I spent eighteen months arguing against them, and eventually I ran out of arguments.
[06:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was your last argument?
[06:56] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Maintenance. It's always maintenance. And it's a good argument right up until the platform also requires maintenance, at which point you're comparing two maintenance burdens and one of them costs a hundred thousand a year.
[07:13] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is that what you're paying Workato?
[07:16] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Less. Not dramatically less.
[07:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So it isn't a price decision.
[07:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's partly a price decision, because at the margin we could justify one and not the other. But no, it's not primarily price.
[07:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then what tipped it to Workato specifically?
[07:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Two things. Their connector for our core banking platform is genuinely better than yours. That one's just true.
[07:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It is true. We know.
[07:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): And their engineering-facing story is stronger. Recipes as code, better CI story, our engineers had opinions about it and the opinions were positive.
[08:02] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So you've bought an engineering tool.
[08:05] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Yes. That's fair. We've bought an engineering tool and stopped pretending.
[08:12] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which is the honest conclusion. My team is never going to build workflows. That was my ambition and it was wrong, and rather than keep paying for the ambition I've accepted the reality.
[08:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask — do you think that ambition was wrong in principle, or wrong for Verity?
[08:33] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] For Verity. I've seen it work elsewhere. I was at a retailer before this where the operations team genuinely did build their own things.
[08:45] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was different?
[08:47] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): There was a person whose job it was. Not a champion, not an enthusiast — a role, with a title, whose entire job was building and maintaining automations for the business. Half a headcount, maybe.
[09:04] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We never had that.
[09:06] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We never had that and I never asked for it, because I thought the product removed the need for it.
[09:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's — I want to write that down properly, because I think it's the most important thing you've said.
[09:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which part?
[09:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That the product doesn't remove the need for the role. It changes what the role has to be good at.
[09:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Yes. That's exactly it.
[09:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): We do say that, in fairness. It's in the operating model guidance.
[09:40] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Is it? I've never seen the operating model guidance.
[09:44] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Then we don't say it, do we.
[09:48] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] Not effectively.
[09:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me ask about the sales process, since I ran it. What did I get wrong?
[09:58] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You want honesty on this too?
[10:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Especially on this.
[10:03] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You sold to my enthusiasm rather than to my capability. I was excited, I said my team would own it, and nobody in your organisation asked "who specifically, and what else is on their plate?"
[10:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a fair criticism.
[10:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not that you lied. You just believed me, and you shouldn't have, because I didn't know what I was agreeing to.
[10:31] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've started asking that question, for what it's worth. Not because of you — I don't want to claim that. But it's in my discovery now. "Name the person who'll build the second workflow."
[10:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's a good question. I wouldn't have had an answer.
[10:50] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the point of it.
[10:52] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I raise the support thing? Since we're doing grievances.
[10:57] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Go ahead.
[11:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The support was inconsistent. Some tickets came back in an hour with someone who clearly understood the product. Others came back in a day with a link to documentation I'd already read and cited in the ticket.
[11:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a known problem and it's a triage problem rather than a capability problem.
[11:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I assumed as much. It's not why we left. But it contributed to a general feeling that we were a small account.
[11:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Were you treated as a small account?
[11:36] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably accurately, yes.
[11:40] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's the answer, isn't it. You were an eighty-thousand-pound account in a book of accounts where that's below median.
[11:50] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): I'd worked that out.
[11:52] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Most customers do.
[11:55] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is there anything we could have done in the last six months? Genuinely, not rhetorically.
[12:02] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably not. By March we'd started the Workato evaluation and once that starts it has its own momentum. People invest in it, they want to be right.
[12:16] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): There was a moment in April.
[12:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Was there?
[12:21] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): When the Workato PoC hit the same connector problem we'd hit with you. For about two weeks it looked like we'd have the same issue either way.
[12:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What happened?
[12:35] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): They put a solutions architect on it for three days and built us a working custom connector as part of the evaluation. Not billed.
[12:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Ah.
[12:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That's when it was over, if you want the specific moment.
[12:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Did anyone from our side know about the connector problem in April?
[12:59] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I mentioned it on a call. Not as an emergency. As a thing I was dealing with.
[13:06] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I remember that call.
[13:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You said you'd look into whether there was a template.
[13:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And I did, and there wasn't, and I emailed you saying there wasn't.
[13:18] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You did. That was an accurate and completely useless answer.
[13:23] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Yes. It was.
[13:26] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I'm not attacking you. You answered the question I asked. It's just that the right response wasn't answering the question.
[13:36] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The right response was three days of an SE.
[13:40] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The right response was three days of an SE, yes.
[13:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Would we have done that?
[13:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): For an eighty-thousand-pound account at renewal risk? [pause] I'd have had to argue for it. I might have lost.
[13:56] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a thing I'm going to raise internally.
[13:59] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): For what it's worth, I don't think you should have kept us. I think we were the wrong customer for the product, or the product was sold to us for the wrong reason.
[14:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which of those?
[14:13] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Both, slightly.
[14:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Alright. Let me ask about the practical side. What do you need from us for the exit?
[14:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Workflow definitions and run history exported. I've already pulled the definitions through the API and they came out fine.
[14:32] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Run history?
[14:34] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That's the one I want to check. We need eighteen months of run records for audit purposes. Not for Workato — for our own compliance.
[14:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Through the run events API. I'll send the pagination details because eighteen months is a lot of records and people usually hit a limit and assume it's broken.
[14:57] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That would be useful.
[15:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): How long do you need access after the contract ends?
[15:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): When does it end?
[15:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thirty-first of October.
[15:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I'd want until the end of November to be safe. The export will take longer than anyone thinks.
[15:15] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I can do read-only access through November at no charge. I'd rather you had a clean exit than a scramble.
[15:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You'd do that?
[15:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yes, and I'd do it for two reasons. One, it's the right thing. Two, you'll be at another company in three years.
[15:36] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] That's very honest.
[15:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's both true things at once.
[15:42] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): I appreciate it either way.
[15:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And data deletion afterwards? You'll want that documented.
[15:50] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Yes. Our compliance team will ask for a deletion certificate.
[15:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll get that arranged and I'll tell you the timeline for it rather than saying "shortly after termination."
[16:04] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Thank you.
[16:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Anything else practical?
[16:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): There are two workflows still running that we haven't migrated. They'll be done by mid-October.
[16:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What are they?
[16:18] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Merchant onboarding notifications and a daily reconciliation report.
[16:24] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Neither of which will break anything if they stop.
[16:28] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The reconciliation one would be noticed. Not catastrophically.
[16:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll flag them so nobody deactivates anything early.
[16:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask one more question and then I'll let you go?
[16:42] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Go on.
[16:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): If you were advising another operations director who was about to buy a workflow platform — any workflow platform, not ours — what would you tell them?
[16:56] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Three things. First, name the person who'll build the fifth workflow, not the first. The first one gets built by whoever's enthusiastic. The fifth one gets built by whoever's job it is.
[17:12] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's better than my version of that question.
[17:16] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Second — do the integration assessment before you buy, not after. We spent four months discovering that our most important integration didn't exist. That's a question you can answer in a week if you insist on it during the evaluation.
[17:34] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We should have insisted.
[17:37] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We should have insisted and we didn't, because everyone was excited.
[17:42] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And the third?
[17:44] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Third — be honest about whether you're buying a business tool or an engineering tool, because they're priced differently and they succeed differently, and if you buy one and use the other you'll be unhappy for two years.
[18:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the whole thing, isn't it.
[18:03] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's the whole thing.
[18:06] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I add one for the record?
[18:09] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please.
[18:11] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Whatever platform you buy, get the exported definition of a real workflow during the evaluation and have an engineer read it. Not the demo. A real one, with branching. Because that tells you whether you'll be able to review changes, and it takes ten minutes, and almost nobody does it.
[18:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Someone did that to us last month, actually.
[18:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Did we pass?
[18:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] I think so. It's ongoing.
[18:43] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Good.
[18:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Can I ask what would bring you back? In three years, at another company or here.
[18:52] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): An honest answer to "who will build the fifth workflow", and a proposal that includes whatever it costs to make that person real. If someone had said to me "this is eighty thousand for the platform and twenty-five for six months of someone sitting with your team", I might have said no. But I'd have said no with my eyes open, or said yes and it would have worked.
[19:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a product and pricing point, not a sales point.
[19:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's a bit of both.
[19:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's a bit of both. I'm going to take it to our product team, and I'll tell you honestly that I don't know whether anything will change.
[19:36] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's fine. I've been on the other side of that.
[19:41] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. What you'll get from us — the run events API pagination details, read-only access through November, the deletion certificate with an actual timeline, and a note flagging the two live workflows so nothing gets switched off early.
[19:59] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That covers it.
[20:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And genuinely, thank you. Most people don't take this call.
[20:07] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Most people don't ask properly. You asked properly.

[05:22] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Because you can't sanitise it reliably and you'd be making a promise to ninety clients that you can't audit.
[05:31] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): [pause] Good.
[05:33] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Would a summary built from structured fields actually be any good?
[05:39] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Honestly? Probably good enough to save your analysts fifteen minutes, and not good enough to send unedited. Which is what you asked for.
[05:50] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Fifteen minutes times about four hundred incidents a month.
[05:55] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): That's a real number.
[05:57] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I'd test it on fifty historical incidents before believing my own estimate. Generate a draft for each, have an analyst score it, and see whether the time saving is real.
[06:11] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): We could do that with closed incidents.
[06:14] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): You could do it this month, before you change anything in production.
[06:20] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Which model?
[06:22] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): You choose, within what your administrator allows. And the model configuration used is logged per run, so you can evidence which model produced which draft.
[06:34] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): For how long?
[06:36] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Within your configured retention. What's yours set to?
[06:41] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Ninety days, I think.
[06:43] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): One hundred and eighty for anything client-facing.
[06:47] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Then I'd check which bucket run records fall into for you, because that's the sort of thing that's assumed rather than verified.
[06:56] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Add it to the list.
[06:58] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): On the list.
[07:00] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Training. I know the answer but I want it said on this call.
[07:05] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): We do not use customer workflow content to train a shared OrbitFlow model. That's in your contract, not just in the documentation.
[07:15] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): And the model provider?
[07:18] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Depends on the provider and the arrangement. We use enterprise API arrangements where those exist and the providers are documented as subprocessors. I'm not going to make a blanket statement covering every provider, because it isn't true.
[07:35] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Which providers are on the allowed list currently?
[07:39] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I'll send the current list with the subprocessor documentation rather than reciting it and getting one wrong.
[07:47] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Fine. And if a provider changes their terms?
[07:52] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Subprocessor change notification. The notice period is contractual and it's in your agreement.
[07:59] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): I'll look it up.
[08:01] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's thirty days for your contract. I checked before the call because I assumed you'd ask.
[08:08] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): [pause] Thank you. That's good account management.
[08:13] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's the only reason I get invited back.
[08:16] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): [laughs]
[08:18] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Last one on AI. What happens when it's wrong?
[08:23] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): The analyst catches it, because they're reviewing. But the failure mode you should actually worry about is not the obvious error — it's the plausible one. A summary that says the incident was contained at 14:20 when it was 16:20. Nobody catches that by reading, because it reads fine.
[08:44] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): So the control is —
[08:46] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): The control is not putting facts in the summary that the analyst has to verify. Times, asset counts, classifications — those should be templated from the record directly, not generated. Let the model write the prose around fixed facts.
[09:04] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): [pause] That is a very good answer.
[09:08] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): That's better than what our analysts do now, frankly. They retype the times.
[09:14] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Then that's a bug in your current process and you can fix it independently of any of this.
[09:21] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Noted.
[09:23] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Right. I'm supportive, subject to the four written answers.
[09:29] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Which are — AI-step permission granularity, retention bucket for run records, current allowed model list, and the subprocessor documentation.
[09:41] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Correct.
[09:43] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And the fifty-incident test before anything goes live.
[09:47] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): I'll set that up. Two weeks.
[09:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Does that need a commercial conversation? AI usage sits within your run allocation but there's a consumption element.
[09:59] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): How much?
[10:01] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): For four hundred incidents a month it's not material. I'll put a number on it so nobody's surprised, but I don't think it changes your renewal.
[10:12] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Put the number in anyway.
[10:15] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It'll be in the renewal papers.
[10:18] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Good. What's your third thing?
[10:21] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Governance, and it's small but it's the kind of thing that isn't small in eighteen months. You've got six builders and no defined promotion process. Anyone can publish to production.
[10:35] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): That's true.
[10:37] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Is it? Nobody's ever raised that.
[10:41] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): It's never been a problem because it's the same six people and they're all senior.
[10:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's never been a problem yet. But you're a security company with no change control on production automation, and I'd rather point that out than have your own auditor point it out.
[10:59] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): [pause] That's an uncomfortable sentence.
[11:03] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I said it deliberately.
[11:05] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Tobias, why don't we have change control on this?
[11:09] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Because we've got six people and we all talk to each other.
[11:14] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): That's not a control, that's a culture.
[11:17] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): It's a culture that's worked.
[11:20] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): It's a culture that works until someone's on holiday and someone else is in a hurry.
[11:26] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Can I suggest the lightest version? You don't need a full dev-test-prod pipeline for six people. What you need is that publishing to production requires a second person, and that there's version history so you can see what changed. The version history exists already.
[11:45] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Does it? I've never looked at it.
[11:48] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Version history and change metadata on every workflow. You can see what changed and when and by whom.
[11:56] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): [pause] Right. That's useful.
[12:00] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): How have you been operating this for eighteen months without knowing that?
[12:05] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Because nothing's broken, so I've never needed to look.
[12:10] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Which is fair, but it's also the reason I raise it now rather than after something breaks.
[12:17] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Can we require two-person publishing?
[12:20] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Enterprise supports governance around who can publish where, so the mechanism is separating build permissions from publish permissions. Whether there's a formal two-person approval gate specifically — that's the same permissions question I'm already checking. I'll fold it into the same answer.
[12:41] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Five written answers now.
[12:44] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Five.
[12:46] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): You're very willing to say "I'll check."
[12:50] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I'd rather be slow and right. Especially with you.
[12:55] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): [laughs] Especially with me, yes.
[12:59] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Can I raise one thing that isn't on the agenda?
[13:03] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Go on.
[13:05] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): We've had two people ask about a mobile experience. Analysts who want to approve something from a phone at two in the morning.
[13:15] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What's the honest answer, Nina?
[13:18] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): The web experience works on a phone in the sense that it renders. It is not a mobile product and I wouldn't sell it as one. If your analysts need to approve at two in the morning from a phone, that's going to be a poor experience.
[13:35] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Is there a workaround?
[13:37] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): The approval could be surfaced somewhere they already are. Teams or Slack — a notification with the context and an action, rather than a link into our UI.
[13:49] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): We're in Teams.
[13:51] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Then that's the pattern. It's more design work than clicking a setting, but it's the right answer and it'd work better than a mobile app would.
[14:02] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Can you scope that?
[14:04] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I'll include it in what I send. Rough shape, not an estimate.
[14:10] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Two in the morning approvals worry me slightly.
[14:14] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Why?
[14:16] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Because a tired person approving something on a phone is not a control, it's a formality.
[14:23] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): [pause] That's fair.
[14:26] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): What are they approving?
[14:28] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Escalation to the client's out-of-hours contact.
[14:33] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Then it's low risk and it's fine. If it were anything touching client systems I'd say no.
[14:41] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): That's a useful distinction for the design. Some approvals belong on a phone and some don't, and you'd want that decided per workflow rather than as a platform setting.
[14:54] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Agreed.
[14:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Right, I said I'd be quick and we're at fifteen minutes. Let me summarise. Renewal is agreed subject to papers — seven percent, no other changes, AI consumption estimate included. AI goes on in a contained workspace with two builders, after the fifty-incident test, subject to five written answers from Nina. And you'll introduce a publish permission separate from a build permission, once we've confirmed the mechanism.
[15:28] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): That's accurate.
[15:30] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): And the Teams approval scoping.
[15:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And the Teams approval scoping, which is exploratory rather than committed.
[15:39] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): When do we get the written answers?
[15:42] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): End of the week. If one of them takes longer I'll send four and tell you which one's outstanding rather than holding all five.
[15:52] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Do that. I'd rather have four.
[15:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And the renewal papers from me by Wednesday.
[16:00] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Tobias will read them.
[16:02] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): I will read them.
[16:04] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): He won't read them.
[16:06] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): [crosstalk] [laughs] I'll read the numbers.
[16:09] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Read clause fourteen at least. It's the training one and it's the one Grace will ask you about.
[16:16] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): I've read clause fourteen. Three times.
[16:20] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I know you have.
[16:22] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Right. Anything else?
[16:25] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): One question, and it's for my benefit rather than yours. Eighteen months in — what's the thing that's worked best?
[16:34] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): The client onboarding workflow. Without question. We used to take eleven days to bring a new managed detection client live and now it's four.
[16:46] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): And it's consistent, which matters more than the number.
[16:51] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): It's consistent. That's the thing. Eleven days used to sometimes be twenty.
[16:57] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And the worst?
[17:00] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): The fact that I've just found out we have no change control and version history exists that nobody's opened.
[17:08] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [laughs] That's fair.
[17:11] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): It's not a criticism of the product. It's a criticism of us, and slightly of you for not mentioning it eighteen months ago.
[17:20] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It is slightly a criticism of us. I'll take it.
[17:24] Grace Okonkwo (Chief Information Security Officer, Halberd Security): Good. Thank you both.
[17:27] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): Thanks. Nina, send the five.
[17:30] Nina Patel (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Four, possibly. But by Friday.
[17:33] Tobias Lund (VP Service Delivery, Halberd Security): [laughs] Bye.
[17:35] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Bye both.

=== CALL-014 (call kind: churn)
CALL ID: CALL-014
DATE: 2026-09-18
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
CUSTOMER: Verity Payments
INDUSTRY: Payments
COMPANY SIZE: 800 employees
STAGE: Churn post-mortem
DURATION: 21 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Ruth Adeyemi, Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow
- Kwame Boateng, Head of Operations, Verity Payments
- Sarah Lindqvist, Engineering Manager, Verity Payments
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Kwame, Sarah — thank you for doing this. You didn't have to.
[00:05] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We nearly didn't, if I'm honest.
[00:08] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. And I want to set expectations: this isn't a save attempt. You've signed with Workato, the decision's made, and I'm not going to spend twenty minutes trying to reopen it.
[00:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Good. That was my concern.
[00:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What I want is to understand what went wrong properly, because two years is a long time to get something wrong and I'd like to not do it again.
[00:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We'll be honest then.
[00:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please be.
[00:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd add — I took over this account in January, so about eight months ago. Some of what went wrong predates me and some of it doesn't, and I'd rather you told me which is which.
[00:55] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Alright. Where do you want to start?
[00:59] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): With the decision. When did you actually decide?
[01:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Properly? June.
[01:07] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): June.
[01:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Though I'd say the decision became inevitable in about February and it took us until June to admit it.
[01:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): February.
[01:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): February.
[01:21] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a month after I took the account.
[01:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not about you. I want to be clear about that.
[01:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd still like to know what happened in February.
[01:33] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): February was when we tried to build the settlement reconciliation workflow and couldn't.
[01:40] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Couldn't, or found it hard?
[01:43] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Couldn't, in the sense that the effort exceeded the value by a factor I couldn't justify to my team.
[01:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Tell me about it specifically.
[01:54] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Our settlement provider is a mid-sized European processor. You don't have a connector for them. Nobody does, to be fair — Workato doesn't either.
[02:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So what was the difference?
[02:09] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The difference is that we ended up writing a custom integration either way, and once you've accepted you're writing custom integrations, you start asking what the platform is actually giving you.
